requirements.description: Multi-Hand Video Poker deals one common Jacks-or-Better hand and completes 3, 5, or 10 independent result hands from shared hold positions.
requirements.notes: Allocated by GitHub issue #77 for issue #94; the game uses the shared card and poker primitives and a fixed Jacks-or-Better paytable.

requirements.description: Authenticated sessions own isolated reload-safe Multi-Hand Video Poker state, hold selections, recent rounds, and canonical route restoration.
requirements.notes: Normal-user session bindings override caller-supplied player ids, and persisted settled rounds survive backend restart.

requirements.description: Each Multi-Hand Video Poker round uses one aggregate ledger wager debit and at most one aggregate payout credit with idempotent retry recovery.
requirements.notes: Game code never mutates balances directly; retry proof matches player, game, round, and transaction type.

requirements.description: The Multi-Hand Video Poker surface provides complete English and Russian copy and remains usable without overflow across required desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.
requirements.notes: Acceptance evidence covers both locales, all four named viewports, hold and settlement states, and canonical route restoration.

requirements.description: Catalog, contract, browser, and long-suite discovery automatically include Multi-Hand Video Poker with requirement, module, version, and visual evidence traceability.
requirements.notes: The descriptor uses sort order 70 and the normalized tests.game_drivers.multi_hand_video_poker:play driver reference reserved by issue #77.

requirements.description: Multi-Hand Video Poker rejects decoded and string non-finite wager-per-hand values before round construction, state persistence, aggregate debit, or payout handling.
requirements.notes: This closes the independent wager helper that does not use the shared require_amount function.

requirements.description: Multi-Hand Video Poker publishes round preparation, bounded rollback, hold selection, draw/archive results, and wager or payout completion markers through provider-atomic latest-document callbacks without losing sibling player state.
requirements.notes: The provider boundary serializes state only; production remains blocked for a second worker because state and wallet movement are separate transactions. Frozen v1 routes, envelopes, game math, and ledger action identity are unchanged.
